key: And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying: ‘Heal her now, O God, I beseech Thee.’
s: After Miriam is found leprous and Aaron pleads for her, Moses turns to God; Rashi, on Numbers 12:13, reads the prayer’s brevity as care lest Israel say that he stands praying at length while his sister is in distress.
src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Numbers 12:13, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.words: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא הֶאֱרִיךְ מֹשֶׁה בִּתְפִלָּה? שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים, אֲחוֹתוֹ עוֹמֶדֶת בְּצָרָה וְהוּא עוֹמֵד וּמַרְבֶּה בִתְפִלָּה
evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 12:13, ‘heal her, I pray Thee’:] Why did Moses not pray at length? So that Israel should not say: his sister stands in distress, and he stands and prolongs his prayer.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Numbers 12:13 and at [128,13] match). Plain sense faithful to 12:10 to 12, Miriam found leprous and Aaron pleading with Moses. Rashi on 12:13, third lemma ‘refa na lah’, asks why Moses did not pray at length and answers: lest Israel say his sister is in distress while he stands prolonging prayer (Sifrei); he adds a second explanation in brackets, which the sentence does not claim. His other comments on the verse (the courtesy of supplication; ‘lemor’ as asking for an answer) are separate lemmas. The reading is his, at this place, without drift. entry-check ok.
